study.proposed_difference: Four bounded host variants: exact M17 replay; exact M18 replay; M17-live common-state M audit; matched unchanged-gradient N audit. Audit variants have identical code except literal CONFIG row_intervention. They embed both loss implementations with only class/config identifier renaming and compare a round17 primary backward, a fresh round17 repeated forward/backward, and a fresh round18 forward/backward on the same parameters/batch. At calls0/512 capture actual role aggregation inputs and complete G, projection target P, correction and eligibility; compare all-parameter gradients and other-parameter gradients separately. An explicit ordinary Adam optimizer clones LIVE shared category/brand moments for three disposable shadow updates, compares cross-source/repeat gradients/updates/moments and checks the actual host-backward/live step against the original-source shadow. No live gradients or updates are replaced. All probes are candidate-authored and sequential, with source/entrypoint/scheduling disturbance checked by separate exact replays. This is a diagnostic candidate, not a newly claimed accuracy architecture. No new performance improvement is predicted or measured here.
predictions: If historical source behavior is stable, byte-identical M17 and M18 replays recover their respective prior AUC/Logloss and source-specific ranking. If exact replay drifts materially, cross-source aggregate differences alone cannot identify the scaffold. Report every replay including failure, without selecting the replay that best matches history.

At identical live parameters/batch, common-state forward logits and scalar BCE should agree. Exact equality is reported separately from numerical proximity; any nonzero forward/BCE difference is investigated rather than accepted from equal aggregates.

If the scaffold affects backward numerics at a probed state, cross-source q/h/G/P/delta, eligibility or complete gradients may differ. The repeated M17 complete-gradient error supplies an overall numerical reference, not a stage-specific tolerance. Report all errors continuously, including zeros; no post-hoc equivalence or significance threshold is inferred.

If different raw gradients induce an Adam difference at the same moment state, cross-source shared-table shadow update/moment error is nonzero; otherwise raw-gradient differences alone cannot establish optimizer mediation. Actual live versus source17-shadow errors flag optimizer/backend or host-backward mismatch within this candidate code.

Matched N audit should preserve forward/scalar and reproduce historical N approximately if audit overhead and explicit optimizer entrypoint are harmless. Magnitude audit should match the exact M17 replay before its performance is attributed to original M17. No expected positive audit-M minus audit-N effect is imposed after the failed bridge.

Each audit returns exactly63 finite scalars: 28 per training snapshot, coverage/training-call indicators, and five first512 validation input-only checks. Require two completed snapshots; absent snapshots or ignored optimizer hooks are missing/incomplete evidence, not zero-error success.
falsifiers: Any changed sample/data/split/scorer/causal boundary or unauthorized input suspends attribution; repair only via an authorized version and paid reruns, never silently change the frozen protocol.

Different common-state forward/BCE, eligibility, role gradients or correction refutes computational equivalence at that state; actual live Adam versus source17 shadow mismatch prevents treating shadow comparisons as verified live updates.

Cross-source errors no larger than same-source repeat at both probes weaken the hypothesized source-specific local numerical cause; they do not prove equality across all14661 calls or exclude a later divergent operation.

Unstable byte-identical replays or an audit-M departure from exact M17 prevents assigning the historical gap to the new scaffold alone. A failed probe, missing completion, OOM or cap overrun is retained as operational evidence, not a refutation of the magnitude mechanism.

One same-seed positive AUC replay or unchanged raw direction cannot establish repeated robustness, significance, recipient specificity, semantic conflict resolution, or Adam mediation. Failed generic replacements do not refute all generic-scaling rules.
alternative_explanations: CUDA index_add/embedding backward order, asynchronous scheduling or memory allocation changes create intervention-specific roundoff; primary-versus-repeat and exact replay controls help but do not identify all hardware causes.
Host initialization/data-order/checkpoint/numerical settings differ across runs. No host manifest/checkpoint tensors are exported; equal N scores do not prove their equality.
Repeated seed42 selection/checkpoint search favored the original winner. No independent seeds or user-cluster confidence intervals are available in this phase.

Audit probes, class/config renaming, temporary diagnostic-buffer swaps or make_optimizer entrypoint disturb execution. Exact M17/M18 controls and matched N audit expose but cannot eliminate this observer effect.

A one-parameter shadow Adam call may use a different backend/grouping than the full optimizer. Its agreement with the actual live M17 update must be reported; mismatch is not automatically evidence of a source bug.

Any eventual gain could arise from generic Adam moment conditioning rather than semantic conflict or recipient targeting. This audit measures same-state source differences, not a performance mediation experiment.

Two sparse snapshots may miss the first or a later divergence. Gradient checks share helper formulas whose AST identity was verified; no claim of independent mathematical validation or full-trajectory equivalence follows.
